amendments.rule: The correlative particle `μέν` is decided by the English alone, exactly as rule 65 decides an intensifying `καί`: where the ASV writes a word for it — *indeed* throughout the corpus, as `ὅτι τὴν μὲν παράκλησιν ἐδέξατο` → *he accepted indeed our exhortation* and `Ἰωάννης μὲν σημεῖον ἐποίησεν οὐδέν` → *John indeed did no sign* — it is its own `aligned` unit on that word, and where the ASV leaves the correlation unwritten it is its own `unrepresented` unit. Marking the correlation elsewhere is not writing it: the answering `δέ` keeps its own *but* or *and*, and the correlative pronoun or article keeps the *some*, *the one* or *the other* that carries it, so `μέν` is joined to neither, nor to a preceding `οὖν`, which keeps its own *therefore*. Rules 44 and 64 apply this same English-side test to an interrogative particle, and as there the test is the particle's work and never its morph tag: `μενοῦνγε` is a separate lexeme carrying content of its own and is aligned in the ordinary way, as *verily*. A reference comparison will report every `unrepresented` `μέν` as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction. The connective `τε` is decided by this same test, and by the English rather than by the Greek pairing. Where the ASV writes a word for it, `τε` takes that word as its own `aligned` unit — *both* in fourteen corpus units, and *and* or *whether* where the ASV writes those. Where `τε … καί` is spelled out with **two** English conjunctions each particle keeps its own: `ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας` → *whether men or women* gives *whether* to `τε` and *or* to `καί`, as `ἐλάλει τε καὶ συνεζήτει` → *he spake and disputed* and `ἀνέβλεψέν τε καὶ ἀναστὰς ἐβαπτίσθη` → *he received his sight, and he arose* give an *and* to each. Where the ASV writes only **one** English conjunction for the pair, that word is the `καί`'s and `τε` is its own `unrepresented` unit: `ἐθνῶν τε καὶ βασιλέων` → *the Gentiles and kings* and `ἡμέρας τε καὶ νυκτός` → *day and night* leave the first particle empty, as twelve corpus units do, ACT.2.9 and ACT.2.10 among them. A `τε` with no answering `καί` keeps whatever connective the ASV writes for it, as `υἱῶν τε Ἰσραήλ` → *and the children of Israel* does. Do not split one English conjunction across the two particles, do not join them into one unit, and do not reach for `noncompositional`, which rules 39 and 45 reserve for a particle cluster fused with the negative `μή` and for a prepositional phrase. LUK.12.45 gives such an *and* to `τε` rather than to the `καί` and is the one corpus unit reading the pair that way, so follow the majority and say in the note that the other reading stands. A reference comparison will report every `unrepresented` `τε` as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.
amendments.why: The contract names `μέν` but nowhere names `τε`, and ACT.9 carries seven `τε` units in four configurations. The corpus answer for LEMMA=τέ NEXT=CONJ is 27 units in 19 chapters: 14 `aligned` on *both*, 12 `unrepresented` where the ASV writes a single *and* that goes to `καί` (ACT.2.9 and ACT.2.10 carrying that reasoning in their notes verbatim), and 1 `aligned` on *and* at LUK.12.45, which the amendment names as the minority rather than hiding. ACT.9 already reads all seven this way and the BSB comparison reports the two `unrepresented` particles as disagreements, which is the same signature rule 70 already records for `μέν`. Amending rule 70 rather than adding a rule keeps the English-side test for correlative particles in one place, as it already holds `μενοῦνγε` and points at rules 44, 64 and 65.

amendments.rule: Where a textual unit's decision leaves the projection carrying a reading the ASV **excludes**, English that answers to the missing source word is `added` under rule 5, and the note must carry enough for a later reader to check it: the unit id, the reading the projection carries, the readings that remained, and why the word is absent. Rule 12 is untouched — this is the citation, not a second vote on the unit. Two kinds of decision do it and the packet signals only the first. It marks an **underdetermined** unit whose fallback the evidence ruled out `FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE` beneath its variant line, and an underdetermined unit whose fallback is still among the readings the English permits carries no such mark and is not this case; but a **selected** unit carries no mark either, and where the reading it selects is shorter than the one the ASV translated the English is `added` on exactly the same terms, the note naming the selected reading in place of the excluded fallback. So the absence of the mark settles nothing on its own: read the variant line. `ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ` → *by Christ Jesus* at PHP.3.12 leaves *Jesus* `added`, `SBLGNT.PHP.3.12.v007` having kept r01 `Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ` and r02 `τοῦ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ` while the projection carries the bare base the English rules out; the verse-opening *And* of JHN.9.28 is `added` for the same reason, `SBLGNT.JHN.9.28.v029` having kept the connectives of r01 `καὶ` and r02 `οἱ δὲ` against an asyndetic base; and *kneeling down* at MRK.1.40 is `added` on the selected arm, `SBLGNT.MRK.1.40.v057` having selected r02, which carries no participle of kneeling though the ASV translates one. JHN.10.13 is the same shape for a whole clause and is the standard for the note. A textual note the ASV prints of its own — *Some ancient authorities omit the Son of God* at MRK.1.1, *Some ancient authorities omit and kneeling down to him* at MRK.1.40 — corroborates the reading and belongs in the note, but it does not license the status by itself: what licenses it is that no token of the projection answers to the English. Rule 37 is the near contrast and is worth ruling out by name, because the two look alike from the English side: there the licensing token stands in a neighbouring verse, here it stands in no verse of the projection at all. Do not reach for rule 7 to fold such a word onto a neighbouring token — a helper belongs to the word that licenses it, and the word that would have licensed this one is absent — and do not reach for `noncompositional`. Rule 11 does not decide this either way, the ASV italicizing such a word only sometimes. The mirror case is where the projection instead carries source material the ASV did not translate, the reading it carries being **longer** than the one the ASV rendered: each surplus token is then its own `unrepresented` unit and owes the same note. It does not turn on the unit having been decided. ACT.9.12 is the first instance and its unit `SBLGNT.ACT.9.12.v010` is underdetermined, r00-base against r01, the projection carrying `ἐν ὁράματι` where the ASV writes no *in a vision* in that verse, so the preposition and the noun stand as two `unrepresented` units whose notes name the unit id and the readings that remained. Rule 2 is why they are two units and not one: an empty target gives no ground for joining them, and rules 30, 48 and 93 already keep `unrepresented` per token. Rule 12 is untouched here too, this being a statement about what the English realizes and not a vote on the unit. A reference comparison will report every such token as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.
amendments.why: Rule 97's closing sentence said in terms that no corpus unit had needed the mirror case; ACT.9.12 has now needed it, so the sentence was stale and would have left a later pass unsure whether unrepresented-for-textual-reasons is permitted at all. Two things are fixed beyond the citation. First, the old wording tied the mirror to a reading the ASV *excludes*, which fits a decided unit but not ACT.9.12's, where the unit is underdetermined and the packet carries no `FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE` mark — the amendment says plainly that the mirror does not turn on the unit having been decided, and keeps rule 12 disclaimed for that direction as the rule already does for the `added` direction. Second, the old wording said `their own unrepresented unit` for plural tokens, which this chapter read two ways: 9:12 grouped its two tokens while 9:28 split its six under rule 37. The amendment states the per-token granularity that rules 2, 30, 48 and 93 already imply, and the ACT.9.12 patch conforms to it.

conventions: Connective relative recast as an English coordinate or causal clause: the supplied clause-introducer is the relative pronoun's own, alongside whatever personal pronoun realizes the relative, and it is neither `added` nor a rule 88 juncture on the finite verb. hos en paralelymenos -> *for he was palsied* (9:33), hoitines epestrepsan -> *and they turned* (9:35) and hon ... anegagon -> *And ... they brought him* (9:39) all read this way, under rule 40's principle that a subordinating element takes whatever word introduces its English clause. Rule 88 is scoped to a participle converted into a coordinate finite clause and does not reach a relative pronoun; giving the introducer to the verb instead remains defensible and is what 9:39 originally took.

A verbless speech frame whose *said* the ASV supplies is placed by what is left in the clause, and by whether a verb of saying is already spent in the verse. 9:11's ho de kyrios pros auton has a prepositional predicate, so pros takes *said unto* under rule 62. 9:5's ho de has no predicate at all, and rule 56 would fold the verb onto the subject article, but eipen (s001) is already spent on the verse's first speech, so the second *said* is `added` under rule 103. The spent lexeme is what divides the two, not the word order; reading 9:5 as ho -> *he said* under rule 56 remains defensible.

An indefinite tis with an expressed anarthrous noun rendered *a certain N* keeps the whole *a certain* as one `aligned` unit headed on *certain*, and the noun stands bare, whether the Greek writes the indefinite before its noun (9:10, 9:36) or after it (9:33). Rule 58's determiner-to-the-noun clause is scoped to an attributive adjective and does not reach an indefinite, which is a determiner in its own right. The corpus is divided: seventeen units read *a certain* on tis, two more read *a certain man* on it, and ACT.8.36 states the reasoning, while ACT.10.1 gives the noun the *a* for the identical anthropon-tina-onomati frame. This chapter follows the majority throughout.

The chapter has two unrelated runs of untranslated Greek and they rest on different rules. 9:28's parresiazomenos en toi onomati tou kyriou is unrepresented under rule 37, its English standing at the head of 9:29, where it is `added` and both sides carry a note naming the other verse. 9:12's en horamati is unrepresented under rule 97's mirror case: SBLGNT.ACT.9.12.v010 is underdetermined between r00-base and r01, the projection carries the longer reading, and the ASV renders no *in a vision* there. In both, each untranslated token is its own unit.

report: Read the whole chapter dump end to end and worked all 74 candidate groups. Three real inconsistencies found and patched: ACT.9.39, ACT.9.33, ACT.9.12. Everything else in the table is the ASV rendering one word differently in contexts the source licenses.

ACT.9.39 is the doctrinal split. The chapter recasts a connective relative as a coordinate or causal English clause three times and gave the supplied clause-introducer to the relative twice - hos en paralelymenos -> *for he* (9:33) and hoitines epestrepsan -> *and they* (9:35) - but gave 9:39's *And* to the finite verb anegagon as a rule 88 juncture, leaving hon a bare *him*. Nothing in the source licenses the difference: all three are connective relatives realized by a personal pronoun plus a supplied introducer. Patched 9:39 so hon takes the discontinuous *And ... him* headed on *him* and anegagon keeps *they brought*. Rule 88 is scoped in terms to a participle converted into a finite clause and does not reach a relative pronoun.

ACT.9.33 is the second split, on *a certain N*. 9:10 (tis mathetes) and 9:36 (tis ... mathetria) give *a certain* to the indefinite and leave the noun bare; 9:33 (anthropon tina) gave *a* to the noun discontinuously across *certain*. The only difference is Greek word order, which does not decide which word an English determiner attaches to. The corpus answer settles it: 17 units of *a certain* headed on tis plus 2 of *a certain man*, and ACT.8.36's note says in terms that the supplied *a* is the indefinite's helper. Patched 9:33 so tina takes *a certain* headed on *certain* and anthropon takes a bare *man*. ACT.10.1 reads the same construction the other way, so the corpus is divided; that is recorded as a convention rather than promoted.

ACT.9.12 is a granularity inconsistency rather than a wrong edge. en horamati, which the ASV does not translate there, stood as one two-token unrepresented unit, while 9:28's six untranslated tokens each stand as their own unit. An empty target gives no ground for joining, and rules 2, 30, 48 and 93 keep unrepresented per token, so the pair is now two units. The rule 97 mirror reading itself is right and is left as the verse pass had it.

Checked and found not to be splits: te (7 units, matching the corpus exactly - two English conjunctions split across te and kai at 9:2, 9:18 and 9:29, one conjunction given to kai with te unrepresented at 9:15 and 9:24); preverb particles and compound-verb datives, which are uniform after 9:39's own correction (proselthon 9:1, synodeuonton 9:7, synelthen and parestesan 9:39 all leave the case preposition with the governed word); article before a name; rule 86 subordinators on participles; rule 88 junctures on the verb introduced; egeneto plus a supplied complementizer (9:3, 9:37, 9:43 all place it on the non-finite complement); archiereus, anablepo, epikaloumenous under rules 90 and 32, and the *for ... sake* / *for ... intent* heads at 9:16 and 9:21, which agree under rule 78. parresiazomai at 9:27 heads on *boldly*, matching both corpus units.

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error. 9:28's six tokens are rule 37 versification, with the English added at the head of 9:29 and both sides noted. 9:12's en horamati is rule 97's mirror case, the projection carrying material the ASV does not render. 9:33's epi and ex are rule 36 (absorbed into *kept his bed* and written with no preposition in *eight years*). 9:13's tois is rule 20, displaced by sou. 9:15 and 9:24 te are the corpus's own reading of te ... kai with one English *and*. No accepted edge was changed to improve the rate.

Conventions: four recorded. The 35 repeated notes the validator lists are almost all restatements of rules 19, 21, 23, 51, 86 and 88, which bind every verse already and need no log entry; what is recorded is the four judgments a later reader could not rederive from the contract alone.

Promotions: no new rules. Two amendments - rule 70 widened to decide te by the English alone (27 corpus units, 7 in this chapter), and rule 97's mirror clause given its first worked instance and a per-token granularity statement.
